text:
micah: hey team, saw flakiness in the eval runner on the quantized bert bring-up. I ran the same seed twice and got different sampled outputs for some examples when top_p was enabled.

olivia: ugh, that's bad. same binary + same weights? any trace/logs?

micah: yep same docker image. logging attached (snippet):
```
EVAL START seed=42 model=quant-bert-v2
example_id=1234 out1="the cat sat on the mat"
example_id=1234 out2="the cat sat on the rug"
```
Only differs for examples with sampling params top_p=0.9 temp=0.7. deterministic greedy outputs identical.

raj: could be worker-level RNG vs request-level seeding. If workers are long-lived and we seed only at init, interleaved batches can consume RNG bytes differently between runs.

micah: that's my suspicion too. we do per-worker seed = global_seed ^ worker_id currently. but batching order changed across runs which shifted RNG consumption.

sam: quick workaround: set per-request RNG state derived from (global_seed, request_id) so sampling only depends on request ordering, not batch micro-scheduling. but that'll add overhead.

olivia: overhead ok for eval infra. more important is reproducibility for CI. can we add deterministic counter-based RNG like philox per-token position?

raj: philox would be ideal. it's a counter RNG so it's independent of consumption order if we index by (request_pos, sample_step). we'd need to instrument C++ sampler to accept a counter seed.

micah: created a small repro script that toggles top_p vs top_k and shows nondet:
```
# python repro
for mode in ["top_k", "top_p"]:
    for run in range(2):
        print(run, sampler.sample(seed=42, mode=mode, n=5))
```
Top_k stable, top_p diverges between runs.

eval-runner: CI noticed flake: job eval/integration/test_samples - flaky on quantized path. Marked by ci-bot as unstable. See https://ci.internal/reports/8923

ci-bot: flaky test detected (eval/integration/test_samples). 3 failures in last 10 runs. Investigators: @micah @raj

sam: another angle: our top_p implementation uses cumulative prob and then a second RNG for tie-breaking when truncation happens. If that second RNG is drawn from the global stream, it will shift consumption. Need to ensure all sampling draws come from same deterministic stream or use independent counters per draw.

olivia: good point. also quant kernels reorder operations for vectorized perf; that might change draw counts across threads. we should treat quantized and fp kernels the same in terms of RNG calls.

raj: plan proposal: 1) short term: seed per-request using hash(global_seed, request_uuid) and force single-threaded sampling in eval CI. 2) mid term: add philox counter-based RNG and expose token_index-based counters in C++ sampler. 3) add unit test in runner that runs 50 deterministic seeds and asserts bitwise identical outputs when sampling params fixed.

micah: +1. I'll open a PR for (1) today, add a flag --eval-deterministic to CI job. I'll also start a design doc for philox integration.

olivia: can you add a reproducibility test to the nightly perf job too? if we detect divergence after a model update we'll fail the rollout.

micah: yes. adding to checklist. Also logging action: add per-sample RNG index dump when --debug-rng enabled so we can postmortem the exact draw counts.

sam: FYI we saw a similar bug when batching with caching enabled — prefix cache reapplies kv-cache and changes sample lengths, which alters RNG draws. keep that in mind.

micah: noted. thanks all. I'll ping when PR ready.

olivia: thanks — labelling this high-priority for eval infra. :white_check_mark:
